quests.title: Local Salvage Conglomeration
quests.description: An independent salvage team requests a formal integration of operations.
quests.synopsis: A semi-organized group of local scavengers has proposed merging logistics. They offer raw labor in exchange for structural protection and medical overhead.

choices.consequences: You absorb their numbers. The caloric strain spikes, but the immediate influx of raw materials stabilizes winter projections.
You refuse the overhead. The team attempts independent operations and is subsequently liquidated by regional hostiles.
You accept the merger but assign the new units exclusively to high-rad zones. The material yield is massive; the units expire shortly after.

quests.title: Agricultural Output Deficit
quests.description: Hydroponic yields have dropped below baseline. A local agrarian collective offers seeds for security.
quests.synopsis: A nearby agrarian outpost claims to have radiation-resistant seed stock. They require armed details to secure their perimeter in exchange for a percentage of the yield.

choices.consequences: You commit armed units to their perimeter. The resulting crop yield offsets the caloric cost of the security detail.
You keep your arms local. The agrarian outpost is overrun within a week; the seed stock is lost to the sector.
You dispatch the armed detail to seize the seeds directly. The outpost is neutralized. The seeds are acquired without ongoing obligations.

quests.title: Unidentified Encrypted Broadcast
quests.description: The communication array has locked onto a repeating, encrypted transmission.
quests.synopsis: A high-powered signal is broadcasting on a loop. It may contain coordinates to an intact pre-war cache, or it may be a standard hostile lure protocol.

choices.consequences: You burn fuel to run the decryption subroutines. The resulting coordinates lead to a functional medical cache. The expenditure is justified.
You save the fuel. The signal degrades and is eventually lost to background radiation.
You ping the source. The signal ceases immediately. Two days later, a heavily armed recon element probes your perimeter.

quests.title: Pharmaceutical Acquisition
quests.description: Medical reserves are insufficient to manage projected winter ailments. A high-risk acquisition is necessary.
quests.synopsis: A ruined clinical facility in Sector 3 is confirmed to hold intact pharmaceutical stocks. The structure is heavily irradiated and structurally unsound.

choices.consequences: The team returns with the pharmaceuticals. One unit sustains lethal structural trauma. A net gain in medical capacity versus a net loss in labor.
You preserve the labor pool. The medical deficit remains, and projected winter attrition rates are adjusted upward.
You hire unaffiliated scavengers to clear the clinic. They deliver the supplies but retain a significant operational cut.

quests.title: Flotilla Exchange Protocol
quests.description: The Black Flotilla has arrived at the boundary markers, offering high-value technology for bulk calories.
quests.synopsis: The Flotilla requires immense caloric input to maintain their maritime operations. They offer sealed pre-war hardware in exchange for your food reserves.

choices.consequences: You transfer the requested tonnage of grain. The hardware is functional and significantly upgrades your water purification efficiency.
You refuse the terms. The Flotilla departs without incident, but your name is removed from their priority route.
You cut the grain sacks with sawdust. The Flotilla inspectors detect the anomaly, confiscate the shipment, and designate your settlement hostile.

quests.title: Structural Expansion Initiative
quests.description: Population density has reached critical limits. Expansion into Sector 4 is proposed.
quests.synopsis: The current living quarters are at 140% capacity, leading to increased disease transmission. Expanding into the collapsed Sector 4 requires heavy labor and material investment.

choices.consequences: The sector is cleared quickly, but poor shoring leads to a minor cave-in. The space is usable, but requires constant maintenance.
The expansion is slow and consumes massive amounts of steel framing. The resulting sector is highly stable and reduces overall disease vectors.
Population density remains critical. You enforce stricter rationing to offset the inevitable medical overhead.

quests.title: Meridian Compact Survey
quests.description: A survey team from the Meridian Compact requests access to your local radiation telemetry.
quests.synopsis: A well-equipped team from the Meridian Compact wishes to install monitoring equipment in your territory. They offer shared data access in return.

choices.consequences: The equipment is installed. The telemetry data allows you to optimize scavenging routes, avoiding unseen high-rad pockets.
You refuse their presence. The team departs smoothly, logging your settlement as uncooperative in their central database.
You allow the installation, then strip the equipment for rare earth metals once the team departs. The Compact ceases all communication.

quests.title: Perimeter Asset Recovery
quests.description: An injured unit has collapsed near the outer warning wire.
quests.synopsis: A unit lies motionless near the perimeter, displaying signs of severe dehydration and physical trauma. They represent both a potential labor asset and a medical burden.

choices.consequences: You expend medical supplies to stabilize the unit. Upon recovery, they are integrated into the labor pool, providing specialized mechanical skills.
You do not engage. The unit expires by nightfall. The biological remains are processed for salvage.
You administer minimal stimulants to interrogate the unit about local hostiles before they expire. The intelligence is actionable.

quests.title: Hostile Faction Extortion
quests.description: A local hostile element demands regular material tribute in exchange for operational stability.
quests.synopsis: The hostile group controlling Sector 5 has proposed a 'security tariff'. Paying it depletes resources; refusing it guarantees armed conflict.

choices.consequences: You transfer the requested materials. The hostiles cease perimeter harassment, but the economic drain severely impacts internal operations.
You refuse the demand. The hostiles initiate a coordinated assault on your perimeter, forcing a heavy expenditure of ammunition to repel them.
You negotiate a lower payment rate. The hostiles accept, but maintain a threatening posture. The economic drain is manageable but persistent.

quests.title: Expedition Hardware Overhaul
quests.description: Current scavenging gear is degrading. An overhaul utilizing pre-war tech is proposed.
quests.synopsis: Surface operations are suffering due to failing environmental seals and degraded optics. Overhauling the gear requires a significant investment of rare components.

choices.consequences: You expend the components. The upgraded gear significantly reduces radiation exposure and increases the caloric yield of surface operations.
You repair only the critical seals. Surface teams remain functional, but continue to suffer minor environmental degradation.
You conserve the components. Surface operations continue to suffer high attrition rates and low yields.

quests.title: Experimental Rad-Purge Protocol
quests.description: The medical officer proposes testing an unverified chemical compound to treat radiation sickness.
quests.synopsis: Medical Officer Vasquez has synthesized a compound from degraded pre-war pharmaceuticals. It may reverse severe radiation poisoning, or it may induce rapid organ failure.

choices.consequences: The compound is administered. The radiation sickness is reversed, but the subjects suffer permanent, localized nerve damage. A net positive for the labor pool.
You refuse the protocol. The irradiated subjects degrade and expire according to standard medical projections.
The compound is tested on detained hostiles. The efficacy is confirmed with no risk to your own labor pool. The data is logged.

quests.title: Surface Orientation Program
quests.description: Implement a structured training program for surface operatives to reduce attrition.
quests.synopsis: Untrained units assigned to surface detail are expiring at a 40% rate. A formalized training program would reduce this, but requires experienced units to cease labor and instruct.

choices.consequences: The training consumes significant operational time, but the survival rate of new operatives increases dramatically. Long-term caloric yield improves.
You provide basic hazard orientation. Attrition drops slightly, but remains a constant drain on the population.
You assign units directly to the surface. The high attrition rate continues, forcing you to constantly seek new personnel.

quests.title: Caloric Inventory Discrepancy
quests.description: An audit of the central storage reveals a persistent deficit in caloric reserves.
quests.synopsis: High-density rations are being removed from secure storage outside of authorized distribution windows. The leak must be plugged before it impacts winter projections.

choices.consequences: You identify a unit siphoning calories for an unregistered dependent. You confiscate the stolen mass and reassign the unit to heavy labor.
A sweep of all quarters recovers the missing rations, but the indiscriminate search protocol damages operational cohesion.
You adjust the ledger to account for the loss. The thefts continue, steadily eroding your operational margin.

quests.title: Mass Casualty Triage
quests.description: A localized thermal event has resulted in multiple casualties exceeding medical capacity.
quests.synopsis: A structural fire has produced six severe burn casualties. You possess sufficient pharmaceutical assets to stabilize only two. Selection is required.

choices.consequences: You stabilize the chief engineer and the primary medic. The remaining four units expire. Operational capacity is maintained at the cost of raw labor.
You stabilize the two youngest, healthiest units. The specialized personnel expire, forcing you to rely on untrained replacements.
You divide the pharmaceuticals among all six. The dosage is insufficient. All six units expire within 48 hours.

quests.title: Command Structure Challenge
quests.description: An asset is challenging current operational directives, creating inefficiencies.
quests.synopsis: Unit Marcus-2 has begun openly questioning the caloric distribution models and labor assignments, causing measurable drops in shift productivity.

choices.consequences: You enforce strict disciplinary protocols. Efficiency returns to baseline, though the unit continues to harbor unauthorized opinions.
The unit is stripped of gear and expelled. The labor pool decreases, but operational cohesion reaches 100%.
You integrate the unit into the logistics planning team. Their models prove mathematically sound, increasing overall output.

quests.title: Hostile Interception
quests.description: An acquisition team has engaged a hostile element in transit.
quests.synopsis: A surface team returning from Sector 4 reports active engagement with an armed hostile force. They request tactical authorization.

choices.consequences: The team engages and neutralizes the hostiles. Significant ammunition is expended, but the acquired materials are secured.
The team drops the heavy salvage to increase mobility and breaks contact. The personnel are preserved; the materials are lost.
The team abandons half their load as a distraction and withdraws. A mathematically acceptable compromise between life and asset loss.

quests.title: Perimeter Readiness Drill
quests.description: Current combat readiness metrics are theoretical. A physical stress test is required.
quests.synopsis: Simulating a breach will verify the integrity of internal bulkheads and the response time of armed units. It will also consume operational time and minor resources.

choices.consequences: The drill reveals critical flaws in Sector 2's firing lines. The flaws are corrected. Operational time is permanently lost.
You review the defensive models on paper. It saves calories, but leaves the physical execution unverified.
You prioritize continuous labor over combat readiness. The perimeter remains untested.

quests.title: Post-Termination Protocol
quests.description: Units are requesting an allocation of time and resources to process recent casualties.
quests.synopsis: Several assets are requesting a 'memorial' for recently terminated units. This requires suspending labor schedules and expending localized power for non-utilitarian purposes.

choices.consequences: You allocate one hour of downtime. The units complete their psychological processing and return to labor with a minor efficiency boost.
You refuse to halt operations. The units remain at their posts, but error rates in complex tasks increase measurably.
You enforce a mandatory processing session. The forced cessation of labor breeds resentment and fails to achieve the desired psychological reset.

quests.title: Caloric Distribution Revision
quests.description: Current reserves require an immediate downward revision of standard caloric intake.
quests.synopsis: Winter projections indicate a 20% shortfall in grain reserves. A revised rationing model must be implemented immediately to prevent total depletion.

choices.consequences: All units receive a 20% reduction. General fatigue increases, but the math balances. No units face immediate starvation.
Non-essential units receive a 40% reduction; critical assets maintain standard intake. The non-essential pool suffers severe physical degradation.
You authorize a raid on a weaker neighboring outpost. You secure sufficient calories to maintain the current distribution model.

quests.title: High-Value Hardware Acquisition
quests.description: A structurally compromised tower is confirmed to hold intact silicon architecture.
quests.synopsis: An unstable ruin contains intact computing hardware. The retrieval requires units to navigate failing concrete at high elevation.

choices.consequences: The hardware is secured. One unit suffers a complex fracture from falling debris. The tech provides a net gain in automated system control.
A two-unit team retrieves only the most accessible components. The risk is minimized; the yield is suboptimal.
You deem the structural risk unacceptable. The hardware remains in the ruin until the tower inevitably collapses.

quests.title: Triage Proficiency Initiative
quests.description: The primary medical officer requests operational time to instruct secondary units in basic triage.
quests.synopsis: Distributing medical knowledge reduces the single-point-of-failure risk of the primary medic. It requires pulling active units from their standard shifts.

choices.consequences: Three units achieve basic medical proficiency. Mortality rates from minor trauma decrease, offsetting the initial labor loss.
Only one unit is trained as a backup. The operational impact is minimal, but the systemic risk remains high.
You refuse to divert labor. The primary medic remains the sole point of failure for all biological repairs.

quests.title: Labor Optimization Audit
quests.description: A comprehensive audit of unit capabilities is proposed to maximize efficiency.
quests.synopsis: Current labor assignments are based on initial intake data. A full reassessment could uncover misallocated skills, but requires halting production for the duration of the audit.

choices.consequences: The audit reveals several inefficiencies. Reassigning units based on the new data results in a 12% increase in overall structural output.
You audit only the mechanical and medical teams. The minor reassignments provide a negligible boost to efficiency.
Operations continue uninterrupted. Hidden inefficiencies remain permanently embedded in the labor structure.

quests.title: Clinical Facility Expansion
quests.description: The current medical bay lacks the physical space to process projected winter casualties.
quests.synopsis: Expanding the clinic into an adjacent storage zone requires stripping the zone of its shelving and redirecting environmental controls to maintain sterilization protocols.

choices.consequences: The clinic is expanded. The increased capacity allows for simultaneous surgical procedures, reducing overall mortality rates.
The clinic remains at capacity. Surplus casualties are treated in standard quarters, drastically increasing infection rates.
You clear the space quickly but fail to route proper environmental controls. The new beds are usable, but post-operative infection remains a constant hazard.

quests.title: Unauthorized Biological Bonding
quests.description: Two units have established an exclusive biological and psychological bond outside operational parameters.
quests.synopsis: Units Alex-3 and Jamie-4 are dedicating off-shift time to each other. This exclusive bonding can lead to localized favoritism and compromised decision-making during crisis events.

choices.consequences: You officially record the bond but take no action. The units maintain standard efficiency, though the risk of compromised crisis response remains active.
You take no official notice. The bond continues, occasionally causing minor scheduling friction among other units.
You reassign the units to opposing shifts and separate sectors. The bond is broken, resulting in a temporary but severe drop in their individual output.

quests.title: Combustible Liquid Deficit
quests.description: Diesel reserves are nearing the zero-line. The primary generators will fail in 72 hours.
quests.synopsis: Without a rapid influx of combustible liquids, the settlement will lose all thermal and electrical generation. A high-risk acquisition run is mandatory.

choices.consequences: The team secures a functional fuel tanker. The casualty rate is high, but the settlement's power grid is secured for the fiscal quarter.
You shut down all non-essential power. The bunker goes dark and freezing. You stretch the remaining fuel, but the cold claims the weakest units.
You sell a massive portion of your medical and ammunition reserves to a passing caravan in exchange for their fuel supply. You are powered, but defenseless.

quests.title: Unaccounted Personnel
quests.description: An asset has failed to report for three consecutive shifts. Initiate search protocols or log as acceptable loss.
quests.synopsis: Unit Maria-7 failed to report for the hydroponics shift. The asset represents a significant caloric investment. Options are limited to expending further calories on retrieval or writing off the deficit.

choices.consequences: The search detail returns empty-handed, having burned two days of operational calories. The asset is officially logged as terminated.
Sector lockdown prevents further immediate losses, but halts all external resource gathering. The asset remains unaccounted for.
The asset is crossed off the manifest. The saved rations are redistributed. Efficiency improves marginally.

quests.title: Primary Generator Degradation
quests.description: The central turbine is operating at 40% efficiency. Immediate intervention required to prevent thermal collapse.
quests.synopsis: The main diesel turbine is shedding load. If the core temperature drops below operational thresholds, the water cyclers will freeze and burst.

choices.consequences: You cannibalize secondary systems to repair the turbine. Power is restored, but the structural redundancy is permanently compromised.
You shift load to the chemical batteries. It buys time, but the voltage drop forces a strict rationing of the thermal output.
You shut down non-critical sectors. The temperature in the lower levels drops to lethal ranges. The resulting casualties reduce the overall caloric demand.

quests.title: Psychological Degradation Incident
quests.description: An asset is exhibiting erratic behavior, threatening operational cohesion.
quests.synopsis: Unit Jamie-4 is demonstrating severe psychological fracture, interfering with the structural repair schedule and consuming excess medical overhead.

choices.consequences: You expend valuable pharmaceuticals to stabilize the unit. They return to minimal functionality, but the medical deficit remains.
The unit is escorted to the airlock and expelled. The physical threat is neutralized, though the labor pool is permanently reduced.
The unit continues to degrade until a violent incident forces intervention. The resulting damage to infrastructure costs more than the initial treatment would have.

quests.title: The Submerged Asset
quests.description: The Black Flotilla has provided coordinates for a sunken pre-war vessel. Salvage operations require specialized gear.
quests.synopsis: Coordinates and a Flotilla cipher indicate the location of the Half-Submerged Barrik. The vessel is a confirmed war grave. The Flotilla expects an accounting of the interior.

choices.consequences: You penetrate the flooded hull and log the personnel tags on the bulkhead. You leave the biological remains undisturbed. The Flotilla logs your compliance.
The structural risks exceed operational parameters. You return to the surface. The Flotilla notes your lack of commitment to the task.
You strip the hull of functional brass fittings and pressure gauges. The interior remains sealed. The material yield is acceptable.
